This period coincides with our cart-checkout surge and resulted in ~6% abandoned checkouts on the promo page.

Attached: telemetry snapshot and the small alert bundle from our side. Ops team flagged the paths with small prompt lengths that we thought would be cheap — appears queueing/backpressure is the culprit.

Can you confirm whether this is a routing/concurrency cap issue on your side or something upstream? We are in the middle of the campaign and need an ETA for mitigation.

Sasha

Subject: Re: sudden promo spike causing long completion queues (SLA variance)

Marcus / team —

Collected metrics (attached CSV). Quick observations:
- Per-worker queue depth spiked from median 2 -> peak 18 for the model shard serving their route.
- Autoscaler added nodes at 00:08, but new workers had cold KV caches; the warmup added ~300ms each request for the first 50 completions on the new workers.
- Circuit-breaker (per-tenant concurrency throttle) did fire briefly at 00:05 for ~90s; policy was the default soft-cap (85 concurrent tokens) rather than hard cap.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: combination of request fanout from the checkout orchestration + autoscaler-induced cold workers caused transient backlog. When the circuit-breaker tripped, some requests were queued on existing workers longer than expected, producing the observed long-tail.

Next steps I recommend (short window):
1) Temporarily relax the soft concurrency cap for FastRetail during their peak windows (we can do for the next 48 hours while we instrument better).
2) Enable aggressive KV pre-warm on autoscaled add events for their model variant to avoid the cold-worker penalty.
3) Add a routing rule to limit fanout for small prompts to dedicated fast-path shards.

I can implement (1) and (2) now if Marcus approves.

Monica
Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: SLA variance: promo-induced completion queue — urgent sync

Sasha / FastRetail —

Thanks for the data and patience. Internal findings: transient queue buildup driven by rapid fanout + cold autoscaled workers; the per-tenant soft concurrency cap also contributed to queuing pressure. Monica implemented the short-lived mitigations we discussed:
- Soft cap relaxed to 120 for the next 48 hours (we’ll monitor).
- KV pre-warm turned on for autoscale events for the FastRetail model variant.
- Routing rule applied to favor dedicated fast-path shards for small prompts (promo/checkout) to reduce extra fanout.

Expected customer-facing impact: we anticipate p95/p99 to return to baseline within the next 60–90 minutes; we’ll monitor closely and update you. Action items for FastRetail ops: please share the promo cadence over the next 24 hours so we can pre-allocate burst capacity proactively.

We also captured logs and put a snapshot in the attached archive for your engineers.

Laura Bennett
